glossary.definition: Action to eliminate a detected nonconformity (ISO 9000 as quoted in the ISO/IAF APG paper).
Action to eliminate the cause of a nonconformity and prevent recurrence.
Immediate steps that limit the effect of a finding while its cause is investigated.
Follow-up evidence check that a corrective action prevented recurrence before closure.
The role responsible for decisions and records in the defined workflow.
Non-fulfillment of a requirement (ISO 9000 as cited in the APG paper).
Requirements without which the CAPA workflow fails, such as linking findings to specific requirements or separating implementation and verification roles.
A vendor evaluation session structured around the buyer's workflow decision sequence and anonymized representative data rather than vendor marketing scripts.
A workflow permission rule preventing the person who implements a corrective action from approving or verifying its effectiveness.
The ability to reconstruct the complete chronological history of a finding, including containment, cause, actions, approvals, and effectiveness evidence.
A precise, unambiguous statement identifying the requirement that was not met and the nature of the deviation, which directly drives the cause analysis and corrective action.
Multiple candidate explanations for a nonconformity that are systematically recorded and tested against objective evidence before concluding on a root cause.
A missing or unrecorded process parameter or variable identified during an investigation that is logged as a finding to prompt future measurement controls.
A secondary factor or control breakdown (such as a deficient sampling plan) that allowed a defect to go undetected or persist without being the primary failure mechanism.
An action taken to contain or rectify detected nonconforming product or symptoms immediately, distinguished from a corrective action targeting root cause.
Temporary controls, such as heightened inspection or extended containment, put in place to mitigate quality risk while a long-term corrective action remains pending.
Objective documentation demonstrating that an action was executed as described, such as released revisions, training logs, or installation records.

example.label: Illustrative example
example.description: An unnamed Canadian manufacturer evaluates CAPA software for one recurring inspection finding, following it through containment, cause investigation, action, effectiveness review and closure; all situations and records are hypothetical, not customer results.

reviewedChapters.title: Mapping the current workflow: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide page adheres strictly to its assigned scope, chapter plan, and boundaries. All cited primary sources (ISO/IAF APG Documenting Nonconformity and NIST RPD-G-07) are accurately quoted with proper disclaimers, external links match research sources, and internal references maintain appropriate caution regarding software capabilities. The text systematically develops workflow mapping from problem definition through handoff mapping, decision ownership, and acceptance criteria using a consistent, clearly labeled hypothetical machining manufacturer scenario.
decisions: Is this a real nonconformity?
How significant is it?
What must be isolated now? / What is contained, and by whom?
What question will the investigation answer? / Who investigates?
Who does what by when? / Who approves the action plan?
Was the action carried out as described?
Is the finding closed, or reopened? / Who confirms closure?

reviewedChapters.title: Evaluating software capabilities: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The chapter adheres rigorously to its assigned scope and outline, providing practical, actionable guidance for evaluating CAPA software without making unsubstantiated product claims. Citations to ISO/IAF APG Nonconformity Documenting and NIST RPD-G-08 correctly reflect the source materials with appropriate caveats regarding laboratory context and auditor guidance. All four subsections feature clearly labeled illustrative examples centering on the consistent unnamed Canadian machining manufacturer scenario. No unassigned FAQ section is present.
decisions: Confirm or reject a finding as a true nonconformity
Rate significance and route
Record containment as a distinct pre-investigation action
Approve or return action plan
Verify implementation and confirm effectiveness before closing
Reopen closed finding upon recurrence
Score candidate products against must-have criteria

reviewedChapters.title: Recording findings and containment: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide page strictly complies with its assigned scope, chapter plan, and boundaries. All cited primary sources (ISO/IAF APG Documenting, ISO/IAF APG Review and Closing, and NIST RPD-G-07) are cited accurately with explicit contextual disclaimers noting auditor guidance and laboratory service limits. All four subsections incorporate assigned workflow decisions, roles, records, exceptions, and software evaluation criteria. Examples are consistently labeled as hypothetical illustrative scenarios featuring an unnamed manufacturer. No unassigned FAQ section was included.
decisions: Confirm or reject a finding as a true nonconformity
Assign significance rating and workflow routing
Define containment boundary and scope (lots, serial numbers, machines, shifts)
Select and authorize immediate containment action (hold, stop, sort, recall)
Notify internal roles, customers, or suppliers
Approve release of held product or work resumption
Authorize documented override for incomplete containment evidence

reviewedChapters.title: Investigating root causes: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The chapter adheres rigorously to its plan, boundaries, and assigned scope for root cause investigation workflows in CAPA software. Primary source citations from ISO/IAF Auditing Practices Group guidance documents are accurately quoted and contextualized. Workflow decisions, inputs, roles, records, exceptions, evaluation criteria, and scripted demonstration prompts are systematically covered across all four subsections. The hypothetical machining manufacturer scenario remains consistent with preceding chapters, and no unassigned FAQ content is included.
decisions: Determine investigation depth based on finding severity and recurrence
Approve midway modifications to the investigation question
Log missing process parameters as data gap findings
Categorize candidate factors as not able to confirm, possible, or confirmed
Differentiate systematic causes from accidental one-off failures
Accept cause statement or return investigation for further evidence gathering
Flag related equipment, lines, or facilities for wider-impact checks

reviewedChapters.title: Planning and implementing corrective actions: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide page adheres strictly to the assigned chapter plan, scope boundaries, and primary source evidence. Primary citations from NIST RPD-G-08 and the ISO/IAF Auditing Practices Group guidance on reviewing and closing nonconformities are cited accurately with appropriate contextual disclaimers. Workflow roles, decisions, records, exceptions, software demonstration criteria, and labeled illustrative examples are systematically developed across all four subsections without unassigned FAQ content or unverified product claims.
decisions: Classify action as immediate fix versus corrective action
Accept or reject proposed action into the CAPA plan based on root cause linkage
Approve or return action plan prior to execution
Accept or refuse action assignment and proposed deadline
Approve or reject due date extension request with interim containment controls
Authorize cancellation of an action that is no longer valid
Confirm implementation evidence or return action as incomplete
